claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a relatively coarse and heterogeneous grain structure.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating may exhibit Cu segregation.
Annealing at approximately 600°C for 1 hour followed by rapid cooling or stabilization produces an ultra-fine-grained surface layer.
The resulting ultra-fine-grained surface layer has a high density of grain boundaries.
A stabilization procedure can preserve the ultra-fine-grained structure during high-temperature sliding.
Refined grains and their grain boundaries restrict dislocation motion during sliding.
The refined grain structure distributes sliding-induced strain more uniformly and delocalizes plastic deformation.
Reduced localization of plastic deformation lowers the coating wear rate.
At approximately 600°C, the annealed and stabilized coating will have a significantly lower wear rate than the as-deposited coating.
At approximately 600°C, the annealed and stabilized coating will exhibit less localized microscopic plastic deformation than the as-deposited coating.
A stabilized nanocrystalline or ultra-fine-grained tribological layer can be associated with low friction.
The predicted improvements apply only while the refined grain structure remains stable and frictional heating does not cause significant additional grain coarsening.
Excessively prolonged sliding or thermal exposure may cause grain coarsening and compromise the wear benefit.

contradictions.description: The boundary and uncertainty fields limit the prediction to tests in which the refined grains remain stable, but the falsification rule treats post-test grain coarsening as a falsifying result. Grain coarsening would instead place the experiment outside the stated applicability regime unless the claim being tested is specifically that the treatment guarantees stability.
